title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(大澤直樹研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Osawa Naoki)
keywords: Electrical discharges and plasmas 2.Insulation and dielectric phenomena 3.Modeling 4.Verification 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to enhance the development of student's R&D skills on electrical and electronic engineering through the research project on plasma science and high voltage engineering. By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1. find an important problem, 2. create a plan for problem-solving, 3. promote a research project, 4. write a project report, and 5. make a presentation of a research work.
advice: [Projects] (1) fundamental research on non-thermal plasmas and dielectric breakdown phenomena Elucidation of mechanism on atmospheric pressure air diffuse dielectric barrier discharge generation, dielectric breakdown phenomena of solid/gas composite insulation, etc. (2) applications of non-thermal plasmas Ozone generation by non-thermal plasmas, air and water treatment, surface modification of interfacial bonding property of composite materials, plasma catalysis for green technology, bio-applications, etc. [Advice for learning] Close communication with team members or a professor promotes your research project effectively.
books: Textbooks: none Reference books: [1] A. Fridman, "Plasma Chemistry", Cambridge University Press (2008), [2] J. Meichsner, M. Schmidt, R. Schneider, H.-E. Wagner, "Nonthermal Plasma Chemistry and Physics", Chapman and Hall/CRC (2012) Reserved books: none
requiredKnowledge: Fundamental knowledge of electric circuits, electromagnetism, transient phenomena in electric circuits, high-voltage and pulsed-power engineering, and machine tools (drilling, lathe, milling, etc.) are necessary. "High voltage and high current are extremely dangerous. In order to avoid the risk of electric shock, students must follow safety regulations and instructions.

activityGoals.body: To be able to find and explain an important problem.
To be able to create a plan for problem-solving.
To be able to promote a research project.
To be able to communicate with team members and/or professor.
To be able to write a project report.
To be able to make the presentation at PD-III final conference.
